1. PULL PIN
2. AIM AT BASE
3. SQUEEZE LEVER
4. SWEEP HAZARD

fire.exit_desc_1: In a fire emergency, heavy smoke reduces visibility to zero in under 30 seconds. Panic causes confusion — knowing your exit routes beforehand saves critical seconds.
fire.exit_desc_2: Never rely on a single exit path. If flames or smoke block your primary route, you must immediately pivot to your pre-identified secondary emergency path.
fire.exit_title_3: Never Use Elevators in a Fire
fire.exit_desc_3: Elevator shafts act as natural chimneys drawing superheated toxic gases. Power failure can strand the car between burning floors. Always use designated fire stairwells.
fire.place_desc: Point your tablet at the floor or table. Tap the green button below (or tap anywhere on screen) to place the extinguisher.
fire.place_btn: 🎯 TAP TO PLACE EXTINGUISHER ON FLOOR
fire.pass_pull_desc: Tap anywhere to select the pin, then swipe right to pull it out.
fire.pass_pull_badge_btn: 👉 SWIPE RIGHT OR TAP TO PULL PIN
fire.pass_aim_title: A — Aim at Base of Fire
fire.pass_aim_desc: Point your device directly at the base of the fire. Hold steady for 0.8 seconds.
fire.pass_squeeze_desc: Press and hold the button below for 1.5 seconds to discharge the extinguisher.
fire.pass_sweep_desc: Move your device left and right to sweep the fire base. Cover at least 75% of the fire width.
fire.evac_desc_1: Sounding the building alarm immediately alerts everyone before heat spreads. Never delay evacuation to gather personal belongings or tools.
fire.evac_desc_2: Proceed directly to your designated external assembly area. Immediate headcount verification ensures rescuers know if anyone is trapped inside.
fire.evac_desc_3: After using the extinguisher, you must evacuate. Select the safest option:

gas.step1_desc_1: Confined spaces (tanks, sumps, silos, underground pits) trap invisible lethal gases like H₂S, methane, or CO. Low oxygen (<19.5%) causes sudden loss of consciousness without warning.
gas.step1_desc_2: Never enter without a signed Confined Space Entry Permit. Calibrated gas detectors must sample the atmosphere at top (light gases), middle, and bottom (heavy gases) levels before entry.
gas.step2_desc_1: In oxygen-deficient (<19.5% O₂) or unknown toxic gas atmospheres, only a Self-Contained Breathing Apparatus (SCBA) provides clean air. Cloth or dust masks offer zero protection against gases.
gas.step2_desc_2: A multi-gas monitor must continuously alert the entrant to rising toxic levels. A full-body harness and retrieval lifeline allow non-entry rescue if a worker collapses inside.
gas.step3_desc_1: The safety attendant (buddy) remains stationed strictly outside the entrance opening. Over 60% of confined space fatalities are would-be rescuers entering without protection.
gas.step3_desc_2: The attendant maintains unbroken visual or radio communication at fixed intervals. If an entrant becomes unresponsive, the attendant immediately initiates external winch retrieval and summons emergency response.
